function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Reykjavík – Iceland’s Ice‑Hockey Hub** | Why Reykjavík is the top choice | Details | |---------------------------------|---------| | **Home of the National Team** | The Icelandic national team (the “Icelandic Penguins”) trains and plays its home games in Reykjavík. The city hosts the national championships and international fixtures. | | **Facilities** | • **Laugardalur Ice Rink** – the largest indoor rink in Iceland, used for league games, training, and public skating.
• **Hafnarfjörður Ice Rink** – a modern venue that hosts club matches and youth programs.
• Both rinks offer high‑quality ice, seating for spectators, and amenities for players and fans. | | **Local Clubs** | • **Íþróttabandalag Akureyrar (ÍA)** – one of Iceland’s most successful clubs, based in Reykjavík’s neighboring town but playing many games in the capital.
• **KR (Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur)** – a multi‑sport club with a strong hockey section. | | **Events & Atmosphere** | • **Icelandic Hockey League (Úrvalsdeild)** – the premier domestic competition, with playoffs and finals held in Reykjavík.
• **International Tournaments** – the city regularly hosts friendly matches, youth tournaments, and occasionally the **Nordic Junior Championships**. | | **Accessibility** | • **Keflavík International Airport** is just 20 km away, with frequent flights from Europe.
• Public transport (buses, taxis) and bike lanes make getting to the rinks easy. | | **Cultural & Recreational Extras** | • After a game, explore Reykjavík’s vibrant nightlife, cafés, and museums.
• Nearby attractions: Hallgrímskirkja, Harpa Concert Hall, and the geothermal Blue Lagoon (a short drive away). | ### Quick Visit Guide | Day | Activity | |-----|----------| | **Day 1** | Arrive in Reykjavík, check into a centrally located hotel (e.g., **Hotel Borg** or **Radisson Blu**). Evening: walk around the city center, enjoy a local Icelandic dinner. | | **Day 2** | Morning: visit **Laugardalur Ice Rink** for a public skating session or a guided tour of the facility. Afternoon: attend a local league match (check the schedule on the Icelandic Hockey Association website). | | **Day 3** | Full day: attend a national team training session or a friendly match if scheduled. Evening: explore Reykjavík’s nightlife or catch a performance at Harpa. | | **Day 4** | Optional day trip to the **Blue Lagoon** or **Þingvellir National Park**. Return to Reykjavík for a farewell dinner. | ### Tips for Fans - **Tickets**: Purchase online via the Icelandic Hockey Association or at the rink’s box office. Prices are modest, and season tickets are available for regular visitors. - **Language**: English is widely spoken in Reykjavík, especially in sports venues. - **Weather**: Pack layers; even in summer, evenings can be cool. In winter, the rinks are heated, but the city’s streets can be chilly. --- **Bottom line:** Reykjavík offers the best combination of world‑class ice‑hockey facilities, national team presence, local club action, and easy accessibility. Whether you’re a hardcore fan, a casual spectator, or just looking to experience Icelandic culture through sport, Reykjavík is the city to visit.
